content.thinking:
I'm going through each claim in turn: the root cause is attributed to F1, which I'm treating as a hedged, unverified reading, and the plain-words version rests on the T7 detail about a different graphics card, with the "likely rounds" wording kept as a hedge. The still-at-risk point uses "could," which is also hedged and tied to F1 and M.

I'm checking the causal chain claims against the record: the series figures and error rates line up, and the mitigation of moving pods back to V100 cards is confirmed by the timing. The statement that the A100 scorer raised the hold share is backed by that confirmation, but the claim about how the files Code-Fix read change its hold decisions is stated as fact with no hedge, so I need to look at whether that attribution holds.

I'm checking whether the claim that Code-Fix's file reading changes the hold decisions is actually supported, since nothing has run that code. The confirmed mitigation and the timing back the A100 link, so I'm inclined to accept it.

I'm checking the got_lucky point: only the replica that started at the onset landed on an A100 card, while the others stayed on V100s, so the rise lines up with that one replica. Moving everything back to V100s brought the series back to normal, which supports the link, though the record doesn't break holds out per replica, so "confined to" is still an inference I'm weighing.

I'm weighing whether the rise can really be pinned to a single replica: the average went from about 4.7% to 17.5%, and if the other two stayed near their old rate, the one on the A100 would have to be near 43%, which is plausible. The reading that it was confined to that replica still comes from Code-Fix's account, so I'll credit it to the scheduling detail and the timeline, and keep track of that.

content.text:
I found no claim in the document that the record fails to support, so nothing is flagged. Three calls were close, and I counted them as supported:

- **Causal chain 3** says outright that running the scorer on the A100 card raised the share of purchases held. Nothing measured the scorer directly. I accepted it because holding every pod to V100 cards was confirmed to bring the service back to normal (T16, T18, T19).
- **Causal chain 4** states the TF32 rounding without a hedge. It is framed as what the files Code-Fix read do, and it cites F1, Code-Fix's reading of the source.
- **"Got lucky"** says the rise was confined to the purchases that one A100 replica scored. The record has no per-replica figures for this. It rests on T7 (only that replica was on an A100) and on Code-Fix's reading in F1, backed by the confirmed fix.

supported.quote: The fraud model's logit is the small difference between two large products of opposite sign (weights of {F1.1} and {F1.2}).

In src/io_shop/fraud_scoring.py, `fraud_logit` rounds every operand to TF32, which keeps only {F1.3} significand bits, whenever `ALLOW_TF32` is True and the card is listed in `TF32_ACCELERATORS`, and that list holds NVIDIA-A100-SXM4-40GB.

On an A100 the rounding changes each product by more than the difference the decision depends on, so the logit there, and with it the hold decision, is mostly rounding error. It rests on F1, a reading of the source nothing ran, so it is unverified.

One copy of the shop's service started on a different kind of graphics card from the others, and on that card the fraud check likely rounds its numbers coarsely enough to change its decisions, so it held many more purchases for review.
Any replica of the shop that lands on an A100 card again, once its pods are no longer held to V100 cards, could again hold far more purchases for review than its peers.
The shop held far more purchases for fraud review than usual
The shop held a much larger share of purchases for fraud review than before the onset, enough to fire FraudHoldsHigh. Failed requests did not rise.
As read at {T7.1}, the replica io-shop-7d9c4f8b6-x2k9p had started at the onset on an NVIDIA-A100-SXM4-40GB card. The other replicas ran on Tesla-V100-SXM2-16GB cards.
Running the fraud scorer on the A100 card raised the share of purchases held.
Once every pod was held to Tesla-V100-SXM2-16GB cards, the service was no longer at the incident's level from {T18.2}.
On the A100 card, the scorer in the files Code-Fix read rounds the fraud model's weights and inputs to TF32, which changes its hold decisions.
Before the incident, io-shop's pods were held to no card type, so the scheduler could put a replica on an A100 card next to replicas on V100 cards.
No check was seen that the fraud scorer makes the same decisions on every card type it can run on.
The test file's docstring said Ampere behaviour was deliberately left untested.
The FraudHoldsHigh alert paged nobody: no on-call incident was linked to it.
